hldContextSlice.frameworkSummary: Brainstorm ships as a first-class workflow stage (alternative a1): a peer runner directory src/workflow/runners/brainstorm/ that self-registers through the existing executor registry and workflow/index.ts registerWorkflowRunners; a new persisted SpecArtifact peer file in src/workflow/artifacts/ with a specArtifactPaths peer in storage.ts (hash-addressed, listed, approval-stamped identically to DEF/HLD/LLD/PLAN); and an additive elicitation phase on the existing insrc_workflow_step MCP surface that reuses state-store.ts and the questions-gate primitive and preserves the opaque state token verbatim. The single cross-cutting SpecArtifact shape (intent, scope boundary, non-goals, decisions-with-ruled-out-alternatives, open items) is read unchanged by both define (s8) and standalone design.story (s9). Nothing touches the shared/chat-agent brainstorm.addIdea stub.

ownedContracts.name: Approved-spec-as-focus consumption contract
ownedContracts.purpose: The read-side contract by which define and standalone design.story accept an approved SpecArtifact as their focus instead of a raw string, gated on approval (k12) and leaving the plain-focus path byte-identical (k1). Owned where approval lives (s7); consumed by the two seeding stories.

consumedContracts.name: SpecArtifact record + hash-addressed persistence
consumedContracts.purpose: The one durable, structured spec both downstream stages read. A typed record (like define.ts/plan.ts) persisted hash-addressed with approval stamping via a storage.ts peer, so it is listed and approval-gated identically to every other workflow artifact and no consumer-specific variant exists (k1,k6,k7).

boundary.internal: The review+approval wiring for the spec: running the independent review over the sc1 record, enforcing the block verdict, refusing approval without an explicit override, and stamping meta.approvedAt. How the approve gate marks a spec approved is internal; sc4 exposes only the approved-spec resolution other stages consume.

hldContextSlice.rolloutPhase: Phase C — Persist + review/approve the spec

nonFunctional.performance: Elicitation is interactive and controller-paced; there is no daemon-side latency SLA because the daemon runs no autonomous loop (k2). The stage sits on the critical design path and uses the core model tier — correctness of the elicited spec is never traded for fewer or cheaper model calls (k13).
nonFunctional.security: No new external surface. The MCP layer never opens LMDB/LanceDB; the SpecArtifact is read/written only through daemon IPC (k11). The stage is namespaced distinctly from the shared/chat-agent brainstorm.addIdea offlineRpc stub and never invokes it (k10).
nonFunctional.observability: The stage emits the same step-start/step-done/synthesize progress frames as the existing stages, and the SpecArtifact appears in the same artifact listing surfaces, so an in-flight or completed brainstorm is observable exactly like any other stage (ac3).
nonFunctional.durability: The SpecArtifact is hash-addressed and written atomically via the existing storage writeAtomic path; reading it back returns identical content. Approval is a durable meta.approvedAt stamp; an abandoned conversation persists nothing (s3/ac5), and an unapproved spec cannot be consumed (k12).

api.name: readSpecArtifact
api.signature: function readSpecArtifact(repoPath: string, specHash: string): SpecArtifact

parameters.name: repoPath
parameters.purpose: Registered repo root; resolves the on-disk artifact location.

parameters.name: specHash
parameters.purpose: The SpecArtifact identity (meta.specHash, 16-hex) minted by the brainstorm stage in s6.

returns.meaning: The parsed s6 SpecArtifact record (approved or not); mirrors readDefineArtifact/readHldArtifact.

errors.condition: No JSON exists at specArtifactPaths(repoPath, specHash).json.
The JSON is present but its body fails isSpecBody (corrupt/incompatible record).

postconditions: Returns the record without mutating disk

api.name: requireApprovedSpec
api.signature: function requireApprovedSpec(repoPath: string, specHash: string): SpecArtifact

parameters.name: specHash
parameters.purpose: The SpecArtifact identity to resolve as an approved seed.

returns.meaning: The SpecArtifact ONLY when meta.approvedAt is a non-empty string; otherwise it throws. Mirrors requireApprovedEpic/Hld/Lld/Plan.

errors.condition: meta.approvedAt is unset/empty — a distinct named error whose message names the SPEC id and states approval is still outstanding, so the caller relays it to the user (ac4).
The spec JSON does not exist (propagated from readSpecArtifact).

preconditions: The spec has been persisted by the brainstorm stage (s6)
postconditions: A returned value is guaranteed approved (meta.approvedAt present)
An unapproved spec is never returned as a consumable seed (k12)

api.name: specResolveApprovedHandler
api.signature: 'spec.resolveApproved': (params: { repo: string; specHash: string }) => { spec: SpecArtifact } | { error: string; code: 'not-approved' | 'not-found' }

parameters.name: repo
parameters.purpose: Absolute registered repo path (daemon-side resolution; consumers never open disk, k11).

returns.meaning: On success the approved SpecArtifact; otherwise a structured error carrying the outstanding-approval (or not-found) reason for the consumer to surface (ac4). Mirrors the existing 'workflow.approve' IPC shape in daemon/index.ts.

errors.condition: requireApprovedSpec threw — mapped to { error, code:'not-approved' }; a missing spec maps to { error, code:'not-found' }.

preconditions: The daemon owns all DB/disk access (k11)
postconditions: s8/s9 obtain an approved spec ONLY through this IPC, never by reading the artifact file directly

errorCases.scenario: A downstream stage (define s8 / design.story s9) is pointed at a spec that has not been approved.
errorCases.detection: requireApprovedSpec reads the spec JSON and sees meta.approvedAt is absent or an empty string.
errorCases.response: Throw SpecNotApprovedError naming the SPEC id and stating approval is still outstanding; the 'spec.resolveApproved' IPC maps it to { error, code:'not-approved' } and the consuming stage relays that to the user instead of seeding its focus.
errorCases.userImpact: The user is told the spec is not yet approved and no design work is built on an unreviewed spec (ac4, k12).

errorCases.scenario: A specHash is resolved but no artifact exists at that identity (never persisted / wrong hash).
errorCases.detection: readSpecArtifact finds no file at specArtifactPaths(repoPath, specHash).json.
errorCases.response: Throw SpecArtifactNotFoundError; the IPC maps it to { error, code:'not-found' } for the consumer to surface.
errorCases.userImpact: The user learns the referenced spec does not exist rather than getting a silent empty seed.

errorCases.scenario: Approval is attempted on a spec whose independent review returned a block verdict, without an explicit override.
errorCases.detection: approveArtifactByJsonPath reads meta.review and sees a block verdict while no reviewOverride was supplied.
errorCases.response: Approval is refused (the existing workflow-agnostic block-verdict enforcement); the blocking reason is returned in the approve result's skipped[] and relayed to the user.
errorCases.userImpact: A spec the review flagged cannot be approved silently; the user sees why and must resolve or explicitly override (ac2).

errorCases.scenario: The spec JSON is present but its body no longer matches the SpecArtifact shape (corrupt / hand-edited).
errorCases.detection: readSpecArtifact runs isSpecBody on the parsed body and it returns false.
errorCases.response: Throw a plain Error describing the malformed spec record; do not return a partial artifact.
errorCases.userImpact: The consumer fails loudly on a corrupt spec rather than seeding design work from garbage.

edgeCases.input: A spec that IS approved (meta.approvedAt set) AND carries a block review verdict that was explicitly overridden at approve time (reviewOverride recorded).
edgeCases.expected: requireApprovedSpec returns it — approval is the gate, and the override was already recorded on the artifact; the resolver does not re-litigate the review verdict.

edgeCases.input: insrc_review_step is pointed at the spec's SPEC-*.md path.
edgeCases.expected: The workflow-agnostic run-artifact review runs unchanged (stage = meta.workflow = 'brainstorm'), returns findings for the user to resolve, and stamps meta.review — no per-type branch (ac1).

edgeCases.input: A specHash whose slug-named .md was moved/renamed but the hash-named .json is intact.
edgeCases.expected: Resolution is unaffected — requireApprovedSpec reads the hash-named JSON, not the slug .md; only the review step (which needs the .md) would report the md missing.

invariantsToPreserve.text: Consumers reach the SpecArtifact only through daemon IPC ('spec.resolveApproved'); the MCP/consumer layer never opens the artifact file directly.
An unapproved spec is never returned as a consumable seed — approval (meta.approvedAt) is the sole gate, and approval is never auto-granted by the controller.
The plain-string focus path is byte-identical — sc4 is additive; a stage given a raw focus string behaves exactly as before, unaffected by the spec-resolution path.

alternativesConsidered.name: Typed requireApprovedSpec gate-reader + peer daemon read-IPC
alternativesConsidered.oneLineSummary: Mirror the existing requireApproved* family: a typed requireApprovedSpec(repoPath, specHash) in gates.ts that throws a distinct SpecNotApprovedError, exposed via a new 'spec.resolveApproved' daemon IPC (k11).

alternativesConsidered.name: Generic requireApprovedArtifact(jsonPath) + thin spec wrapper
alternativesConsidered.oneLineSummary: Introduce ONE generic approved-read helper keyed on a json path and make sc4 a thin specHash->jsonPath->requireApprovedArtifact wrapper.
alternativesConsidered.reasonRejected: The DRY generic reader drops the typed SpecArtifact return + the distinct not-approved error (partial on ac4/sc4), and refactoring the existing requireApproved* family onto it is M-sized scope creep for an S story; leaving them un-refactored splits the codebase into two idioms.

alternativesConsidered.name: Inline approval-check in each consuming stage start
alternativesConsidered.oneLineSummary: No dedicated resolver — define(s8) + design.story(s9) each read the spec json and check approvedAt inline at start.
alternativesConsidered.reasonRejected: Duplicates the approval check + ac4 message across s8 and s9 (drift risk), risks a direct MCP-layer disk read (k11 hazard), and pushes s7's owned behavior into s8/s9 — violates the HLD story-boundary that sc4 is owned by s7 (scored violates on sc4).
